cards.f: When do you use the sine rule?
cards.b: When you know a side and the angle opposite it (an opposite pair), plus one more side or angle.

cards.f: When do you use the cosine rule?
cards.b: Two sides and the included angle (find the third side), or all three sides (find an angle).
½ab sin C, where C is the angle between sides a and b.
sin θ = sin(180° − θ). If the angle could be obtuse, use 180° − θ and check the angles still sum to less than 180°.

cards.f: cos A is negative: what does it mean?
cards.b: Angle A is obtuse. This is correct, not an error.

cards.f: Which angle is largest in a triangle?
cards.b: The one opposite the longest side (smallest opposite the shortest).

cards.f: Calculator trap with the cosine rule
cards.b: Enter the whole expression at once, e.g. √(7² + 10² − 2 × 7 × 10 × cos 115).

cards.f: Space diagonal of an l × w × h cuboid
cards.b: √(l² + w² + h²). The base diagonal is √(l² + w²).

cards.f: Angle between a line and a plane
cards.b: The angle between the line and its projection on the plane (drop a perpendicular from the top).

cards.f: Area of a parallelogram with sides a, b and angle C
Pyramid with square base: corner to centre
cards.b: Half the diagonal of the base.

short.q: In triangle ABC, A = 40°, B = 75° and a = 8 cm. Find b to 3 s.f.
short.model: b ÷ sin 75° = 8 ÷ sin 40°, so b = 8 sin 75° ÷ sin 40° = 12.0 cm.
points: Sine rule with the opposite pair a and A

short.q: A triangle has sides 6 cm, 7 cm and 8 cm. Find its smallest angle to 1 d.p.
short.model: The smallest angle is opposite 6 cm: cos θ = (7² + 8² − 6²) ÷ (2 × 7 × 8) = 77/112 = 0.6875, so θ = 46.6°.
points: Smallest angle opposite the shortest side

short.q: A triangle has two sides of 9 cm and 12 cm with an included angle of 50°. Find its area to 3 s.f.
In triangle PQR, PQ = 5 cm, PR = 8 cm and angle QPR = 60°. Find QR.
points: Cosine rule with the included angle

short.q: A cuboid measures 12 cm by 5 cm by 4 cm. Find the angle between a space diagonal and the base, to 1 d.p.
short.model: Base diagonal = √(144 + 25) = 13 cm; tan θ = 4 ÷ 13, so θ = 17.1°.
